mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real estate sales (HOUST) indicates a strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods with sustained HOUST increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a reduction in supply, which can lead to increased prices and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong consumer demand and a robust labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% in 1 month AND UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods with sustained PAYEMS increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals inflationary pressures, which can lead to monetary tightening and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods with sustained CPIAUCSL increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% in a quarter signals a weakening economy, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.
